subject: Post-call recap: auth flow, routing & queueing for Dedicated pilot
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@fintegral.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 Jan 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: auth flow, routing & queueing for Dedicated pilot

Alex — thanks for the call earlier. Summarizing the things we discussed and the items we need to lock down to get your Dedicated pilot running: 

High-level ask (what you said)
- Primary workload: realtime payments enrichment + sanctions/risk reranker.
- Target peak load: ~320 qps sustained during batch windows (3 separate service entrypoints).
- Average session: 350 tokens in / 120 tokens out; 85% of sessions under 600 tokens.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 220ms for generator endpoint; reranker p95 < 180ms.

Integration & auth
- You asked about SDK bootstrap path, token rotation, and mTLS as an option for procurement.
- We propose API keys with short TTL + per-route service tokens for the pilot; we can enable mTLS for the production private deployment (requires cert exchange with your infra).

Routing & capacity
- Route by endpoint: generator, embeddings, reranker.
- Autoscale: will provision a dedicated pool and scale by queued requests + GPU utilization; need your input on the allowed concurrency per-session (we discussed 2–4).
- Suggested initial pool: 8 GPUs (A100-equivalent) — we'll provision burst headroom and tune after the pilot.
- Queueing: recommend a two-level queue — fast path for p95-sensitive calls (generator) and a fair-queue for reranks/embeddings.

Structured output & tool calling
- You plan to use structured output + tool calling for enrichment steps. We support function/tool calls and structured JSON outputs; we recommend strict output schemas and guardrails for early fail/validation.

Next steps (owner / ETA)
- Fintegral: confirm expected sustained qps and file the load-profile spreadsheet (you said procurement will attach). (owner: Alex) — ETA: 2027-02-01
- Redwood: produce an initial queue & concurrency sizing proposal plus sample SDK auth flow for your infra. (owner: Sean/Marissa) — ETA: 2027-02-02
- Technical deep-dive to lock routing policy and tool calling patterns (30–45m). (owner: all) — propose Feb 03 or Feb 04

Attachments referenced: fintegral-load-profile.xlsx (you mentioned), redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf (we attached sample pricing/commit tiers).

If any of the summarised numbers above are off, flag them and I will update. Otherwise we'll proceed with the sizing note and schedule the deep-dive.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0187

Thanks Sean — this captures the call well. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirming peak: 320 qps is correct but that's across three logical entrypoints; generator ~180 qps, reranker ~90 qps, embeddings scoring ~50 qps. Spiky windows are 20–30 minutes long during settlement.
- We can get the load spreadsheet over to you by end-of-day Monday.
- Regarding auth: procurement prefers mTLS but they also asked for a fallback plan (API keys with rotation) to shorten pilot start. Can you describe how token rotation would work and whether the SDK has built-in rotation hooks?
- For structured outputs: our compliance team will want validated schemas and an allowlist of tool calls — will that be configurable in the pilot?

Looking forward to the sizing proposal. I can do a deep-dive Feb 3 at 10:00 PT if that works.

—Alex

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: auth flow, routing & queueing for Dedicated pilot

Alex / Sean — quick technical note following up on the pilot design. I put together recommended defaults below so we can iterate quickly when we meet.

SDK & auth
- SDK: recommend SDK v1.4.x (it includes built-in key rotation hooks and an auth middleware you can drop into your token manager).
- Rotation: short-lived API keys (TTL 1h) + refresh token flow. For the pilot we can enable API-key fallback and provide mTLS setup docs for procurement to review.

Routing / routing policy suggestion (example) - Route table:
  - /v1/generate -> pool:gen-fast, priority:high, max_concurrency_per_gpu:3
  - /v1/rerank -> pool:reranker, priority:medium, max_concurrency_per_gpu:4
  - /v1/embeddings -> pool:embeds, priority:low, max_concurrency_per_gpu:6

Autoscale & queueing
- Initial pool sizing: 8 GPUs split as 4 gen, 2 rerank, 2 embed (elastic pools — we can reassign during pilot).
- Concurrency guidance: aim for per-GPU concurrency 3–5 depending on model footprint; we suggest starting at 3 for generator (tight p95 target) and 4 for rerank.
- Queueing: two-tier queue: immediate queue for latency SLO routes (strict dequeue threshold + headroom), background queue for lower-priority scoring. 
- Backpressure policy: circuit-break partial degrade -> fallback to smaller model variant or cached prefix for a % of calls when queue depth > threshold.

Structured output & tool calling
- Schema validation is configurable per-route; we can enforce JSON Schema validation before tool invocation.
- Tool calling allowlist: yes — pilot can run with a strict allowlist. We will show policy examples in the deep-dive.

Operational telemetry we will provide
- Per-route p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, queue depth, per-token cost estimate, and request traces (sampled).

Attachments: I attached a short 'queueing & concurrency' guide (redwood-queueing-guide.pdf) and the sample pricing we referenced.

Proposed actionable items for the Feb 3 deep-dive (10:00 PT)
- Lock per-route concurrency thresholds and initial pool sizes (owner: Redwood)
- Walk through token rotation/mTLS plan with procurement (owner: Procurement + Sean)
- Validate structured-output schema and tool allowlist workflow (owner: Fintegral + Marissa)

I'll draft a one-page sizing note and post it to the shared project link ahead of the call.

—Marissa
